notes: TIER 1 (HTTP fetch): plain curl/WebFetch to www.muji.com timed out repeatedly (schannel TLS renegotiation loop, 0 bytes) while general internet connectivity (google.com, example.com) was fine - this looked like a TLS-fingerprint block rather than a genuine outage, so per the tier ladder I escalated within tier 1 to curl_cffi with a Chrome TLS impersonation profile, which succeeded (200 OK) on every request thereafter; no Playwright/CDP or Claude-in-Chrome was needed. robots.txt (fetched via curl_cffi) has no Claude/Anthropic-specific disallow and does not block the store/cmdty paths used. The JP store (https://www.muji.com/jp/ja/store) is a Next.js/Apollo-GraphQL app; the initial SSR HTML for the store home page ships with the category-nav GraphQL query in a 'loading' state (no data), so the mega-menu/category tree is not visible there. However, individual /store/cmdty/section/<code> pages DO carry a full server-rendered 'sectionTree' JSON blob (department-scoped, code/name/href/children) plus a structured product-count field ('sectionItems':{'total':N}) - this was used as the category taxonomy and qty source (tier-1 structured data, no Playwright needed). Confirmed I was on the real jp/ja taxonomy throughout (breadcrumbs all start '無印良品' > department, hrefs all under /store/cmdty/section/), not a region picker. Departments fully traversed via their sectionTree JSON or full-page keyword sweep: D00056 all of Household Sundries/生活雑貨 (285 nodes: Travel, Aroma/Room Fragrance, Tableware D00046, Kitchen, Towel/Bath/Toilet, Cleaning/Laundry, Interior Goods D00020, Stationery, Found MUJI, Emergency Prep, Bicycle, Green/Gardening/Pet); D00014 all of Food/食品 (134 nodes: Curry, Retort/Freeze-dry, Fermented/Seasoning, Snacks/Confectionery, Beverages/Tea D00030, Frozen/Ice cream D00028, Regional goods); D00055 Furniture/Storage/Appliances (+children D00019 Furniture, D00041 Bedding, D00016 Storage, D00021 Appliances/Lighting/Clocks); D00013 IDEE; and D00001 Women's, D00022 Men's, D00002 Kids, D00025 Bags/Accessories, D00004 Cosmetics (full-page keyword sweep only, as these are outside home-decor scope but checked for completeness). Searched every page/tree for holiday-specific Japanese terms: クリスマス(Christmas)/クリスマスツリー/イルミネーション/オーナメント, ハロウィン(Halloween), バレンタイン(Valentine), お正月/年賀/しめ縄/門松/鏡餅(New Year/Oshogatsu decor & cards), 節分(Setsubun), ひな祭り(Hinamatsuri), 端午(Boys' Day), 七夕(Tanabata), 中元/歳暮(Ochugen/Oseibo gift seasons), 七五三(Shichi-Go-San) - zero matches anywhere. The only 'seasonal' (季節) taxonomy nodes found were all generic, non-holiday-specific: (1) S1070523 '季節食器' (Seasonal Tableware, under 食器/T20014 under D00046) - fetched this PLP directly, structured total=57 products, no holiday-named facets/products inside it (its own product names/descriptions were swept for the same holiday keyword list with zero hits) - this is a rotating-design tableware line, not a Christmas/New Year-branded category, so excluded per the 'seasonal colors/timing, not a specific holiday' boundary rule; (2) S107025011 'エッセンシャルオイル｜季節限定' (Essential Oil - Seasonal Limited) - a limited-edition scent line, not holiday-tied, excluded; (3) S3000234 '季節のお菓子' (Seasonal Confectionery, under お菓子/T30002) - children are flavor/ingredient groupings (potato-chestnut-pumpkin, apple, citrus, mint, matcha), i.e. seasonal-ingredient sweets, not a Halloween/Christmas/Valentine sweets category, excluded; (4) S00708 '季節家電' (Seasonal Appliances, e.g. fans/heaters by season) - excluded, not holiday-related at all; (5) 'D00105/T11002 季節のおすすめ商品' (Seasonal Recommended Products) - a cross-department recommendation/pickup listing referenced only in breadcrumbs of other pages, editorial/merchandising in nature rather than a distinct holiday PLP, excluded. Conclusion: MUJI Japan's own site taxonomy does not present Christmas, Halloween, Valentine's Day, New Year/Oshogatsu, Setsubun, Hinamatsuri, Tango-no-Sekku, Tanabata, or Obon as named product categories anywhere in the departments checked - it uses only generic 'seasonal' (季節) language for rotating-design/rotating-flavor product lines, consistent with MUJI's minimalist no-brand merchandising philosophy which avoids overt holiday theming. No internal site search was relied on for this conclusion (search results are not proof of absence per the rules); absence is based on full department-tree traversal plus full-page keyword sweeps across every major department.
